arxiv-2009-04200.title: Rise of the Machines? Intraday High-Frequency Trading Patterns of Cryptocurrencies
arxiv-2009-04200.creator:
ame Alla A. Petukhina Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin. Firamis GmbH, Germany., 
ame Raphael C. G. Reule Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin., 
ame Wolfgang Karl Härdle
arxiv-2009-04200.description:
A 2020 arXiv research paper by 
ame Alla A. Petukhina Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin. Firamis GmbH, Germany., 
ame Raphael C. G. Reule Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin., 
ame Wolfgang Karl Härdle. This research analyses high-frequency data of the cryptocurrency market in regards to intraday trading patterns related to algorithmic trading and its impact on the European cryptocurrency market.

arxiv-2009-05092.title: Dialogue Relation Extraction with Document-Level Heterogeneous Graph Attention Networks
arxiv-2009-05092.creator: Hui Chen, Pengfei Hong, Wei Han, Navonil Majumder, Soujanya Poria
arxiv-2009-05092.description: Abstract Dialogue relation extraction (DRE) aims to detect the relation between pairs of entities mentioned in a multi-party dialogue. It plays an essential role in constructing knowledge graphs from conversational data increasingly abundant on the internet and facilitating intelligent dialogue system development.

arxiv-2107-11322.title: Sojourn Ruin of a Two-Dimensional Fractional Bronwian Motion Risk Process
arxiv-2107-11322.creator: Grigori Jasnovidov
arxiv-2107-11322.description: Abstract Abstract: This paper derives the asymptotic behavior of \mathbb{P}\left\{\int\limits_{0}^{\infty}\mathbb{I}\Big(B_{H}(s)-c_{1}s>q_{1}u,B_{H}(s)-c_{2}s>q_{2}u\Big)ds>T_{u}\right\},\quad u\to\infty, where B_{H} is a fractional Brownian motion, c_{1},c_{2},q_{1},q_{2}>0,\ H\in(0,1),\ T_{u}\geq 0 is a measurable function and \mathbb{I}(\cdot) is the indicator function. Key Words: fractional Brownian motion; simultaneous ruin probability; two-dimensional risk processes; sojourn ruin; AMS Classification: Primary 60G15; secondary 60G70 1.

arxiv-2110-01110.title: Safe Control with Neural Network Dynamic Models
arxiv-2110-01110.creator: Tianhao Wei, Changliu Liu
arxiv-2110-01110.description: Abstract Safety is critical in autonomous robotic systems. A safe control law should ensure forward invariance of a safe set (a subset in the state space). It has been extensively studied regarding how to derive a safe control law with a control-affine analytical dynamic model.

arxiv-2112-08704.title: Curves over Finite Fields and Moduli Spaces
arxiv-2112-08704.creator: Gerard van der Geer
arxiv-2112-08704.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gerard van der Geer. This survey deals with moduli aspects of curves over finite fields. We discuss counting points on moduli spaces of curves over finite fields. Formulas for the number of points on such moduli spaces lead to modular forms. In this way counting curves and their points over finite fields offers a way to obtain information on the traces of Hecke operators on modular forms. We also discuss stratifications on moduli spaces of curves and their relevance for curves over finite fields.

arxiv-2209-14830.title: An old warm Jupiter orbiting the metal-poor G-dwarf TOI-5542
arxiv-2209-14830.creator: Nolan Grieves ,, François Bouchy, Solène Ulmer-Moll, Samuel Gill, David R. Anderson, Angelica Psaridi, Monika Lendl, Keivan G. Stassun, Jon M. Jenkins, Matthew R. Burleigh, Jack S. Acton, Patricia T. Boyd, Sarah L. Casewell, Philipp Eigmüller, Michael R. Goad, Robert F. Goeke, Maximilian N. Günther,
arxiv-2209-14830.description: Abstract We report the discovery of a 1.32 − 0.10 + 0.10 {}^{+0.10}_{-0.10} M Jup \mathrm{M_{\rm Jup}} planet orbiting on a 75.12 day period around the G3V 10.8 − 3.6 + 2.1 10.8^{+2.1}_{-3.6} Gyr old star TOI-5542 (TIC 466206508; TYC 9086-1210-1).

arxiv-2303-12462.title: Scalable Bayesian bi-level variable selection in generalized linear models
arxiv-2303-12462.creator: Younès Youssfi, Nicolas Chopin
arxiv-2303-12462.description: Abstract Motivated by a real-world application in cardiology, we develop an algorithm to perform Bayesian bi-level variable selection in a generalized linear model, for datasets that may be large both in terms of the number of individuals and the number of predictors.

arxiv-2410-03243.title: Towards TMA-Based Transmissive RIS Transceiver Enabled Downlink Communication Networks: A Consensus-ADMM Approach
arxiv-2410-03243.creator: Zhendong Li, Wen Chen, Haoran Qin, Qingqing Wu, Xusheng Zhu, Ziheng Zhang, and Jun Li
arxiv-2410-03243.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhendong Li, Wen Chen, Haoran Qin, Qingqing Wu, Xusheng Zhu, Ziheng Zhang, and Jun Li. This paper presents a novel multi-stream downlink communication system that utilizes a transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) transceiver. Specifically, we elaborate the downlink communication scheme using time-modulated array (TMA) technology, which enables high order modulation and multi-stream beamforming. Then, an optimization problem is formulated to maximize the minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) with user fairness, which takes into account the constraint of the maximum available power for each transmissive element.

arxiv-2501-01123.title: TED: Turn Emphasis with Dialogue Feature Attention for Emotion Recognition in Conversation
arxiv-2501-01123.creator: Junya Ono, Hiromi Wakaki
arxiv-2501-01123.description: Abstract Emotion recognition in conversation (ERC) has been attracting attention by methods for modeling multi-turn contexts. The multi-turn input to a pretraining model implicitly assumes that the current turn and other turns are distinguished during the training process by inserting special tokens into the input sequence.

arxiv-2511-01832.title: The Double-Copy Root of Hawking Thermality
arxiv-2511-01832.creator: John Joseph M. Carrasco, Yaxi Chen
arxiv-2511-01832.description: Abstract The Hawking radiation spectrum from a collapsing null shell can be derived via the double copy of a simpler gauge theory calculation. Analyzing the non-abelian Yang-Mills root of this process, we demonstrate that the radiation spectrum is thermal in the color charge eigenvalue λ \lambda , not energy.

pmc-10520972.title: Sequential Deoxygenation of CO2 and NO2– via Redox-Control of a Pyridinediimine Ligand with a Hemilabile Phosphine
pmc-10520972.creator: Hanalei
pmc-10520972.description: The deoxygenation of environmental pollutants CO2 and NO2– to form value-added products is reported. CO2 reduction with subsequent CO release and NO2– conversion to NO are achieved via the starting complex Fe(PPhPDI)Cl2 (1). 1 contains the redox-active pyridinediimine (PDI) ligand with a hemilabile phosphine located in the secondary coordination sphere.

pmc-10572162.title: Killer Cell Immunoglobulin-like Receptor Genotypes and Reproductive Outcomes in a Group of Infertile Women: A Romanian Study
pmc-10572162.creator: Mihai Surcel, Iulia Adina Neamtiu, Daniel Muresan, Iulian Goidescu, Adelina Staicu, Monica Mihaela Marta, Georgiana Nemeti, Radu Harsa, Bogdan Doroftei, Mihai Emil Capilna, Gabriela Caracostea, Dah Ching Ding
pmc-10572162.description: A growing body of evidence suggests that endometrial immune disorders may be responsible for endometrial dysfunctions that can lead to gynecological and obstetrical pathology. The aim of this study was to explore the potential relationship between different killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptor (KIR) genotypes and reproductive outcomes.

pmc-11457194.title: Duodeno-duodenal intussusception due to gastrointestinal stromal tumor: A case report
pmc-11457194.creator: Boumeriem Khaoula, Bourekba Iliass, Paulino Insumbo, Nassar Ittimade, Imrani Kaoutar, Moatassim Billah Nabil
pmc-11457194.description: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors, previously referred to as leiomyomas and leiomyosarcomas, are one of the most common mesenchymal tumors of the gastrointestinal tract, predominantly located in the stomach (60%–70%), followed by the small intestine (20%–30%). They manifest at any age but more commonly in patients older than 50 years. Patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumors usually have vague and nonspecific symptoms.

pmc-11499336.title: Resting segmental speckle tracking strain and strain rate in stable coronary artery disease and revascularized myocardial infarction
pmc-11499336.creator: Hatice Akay Caglayan, Didrik Kjønås, Mikhail Kornev, Amjid Iqbal, Mehran Jazbani, Assami Rösner
pmc-11499336.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Patients with acute coronary artery disease (CAD) exhibit reduced global and regional strain and strain rate (S/SR). However, knowledge about segmental S/SR in stable CAD patients is still limited. This study aimed to investigate whether resting segmental S/SR measurements differ in patients with chronic chest pain who have normal coronary arteries or stenotic coronary arteries, and to compare these measurements to those in patients with revascularized myocardial infarction (MI).

pmc-12378186.title: ACLPred: an explainable machine learning and tree-based ensemble model for anticancer ligand prediction
pmc-12378186.creator: Arvind Kumar Yadav, Jun-Mo Kim
pmc-12378186.description: Several small molecules have been approved for cancer treatment, but the continuously growing cancer cases have further encouraged the identification of new anticancer drug compounds. Experimental methods are costly and time-consuming, thus rapid and cost-effective alternative method is much required. The effective identification of anticancer compounds using machine learning (ML) offers a promising solution, reducing both time and cost.

pmc-12575486.title: Vocal mimicry in Corvids
pmc-12575486.creator: Claudia A.F. Wascher, Gemini Waterhouse, Bret A. Beheim
pmc-12575486.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Vocal mimicry, the copying of sounds produced by another species or the environment, is commonly described in vocal learners, such as songbirds. Understanding the functions of vocal mimicry can help to uncover the evolutionary drivers of vocal learning. Different adaptive functions like interspecific and intraspecific communication have been suggested, as well as the possibility of vocal mimicry to be a mistake during vocal learning.

pmc-13202138.title: Psychological self-care, burnout and quality of life among university students in health-related fields across three regions of Thailand
pmc-13202138.creator: Katekaew Seangpraw, Supakan Kantow, Wannita Sakulwattana, Nisarat Auttama, Karnchanok Sukhabot, Sasivimol Bootsikeaw, Boonruang Khaonuan, Parichat Ong-Artborirak
pmc-13202138.description: AbstractObjectivesPublic health students face academic and training pressures as well as challenges arising from patient and community expectations, which may adversely affect their quality of life (QoL) and contribute to burnout and student dropout. This study aimed to examine psychological self-care, burnout and QoL as well as the factors associated with these outcomes among university students.

pmc-13564768.title: Multicenter Validation of Foundation Model Adaptation for Automated Pancreatic Tumor Delineation on CT Scans
pmc-13564768.creator: Halil Ertugrul Aktas, Eminenur Sen Tasci, Linkai Peng, Muhammed Enes Tasci, Yavuz B. Taktak, Sitki Safa Taflan, Baver Tutun, Fergan Bol, Murat Iren, Mucahit Ekici, Andrea Mia Bejar, Elif Keles, Hongyi Pan, Wanying Dou, Burak Gultekin, Alper Akin, Oyku Ikizgul, Okan Cetin, Emre Uysal, Maide Mureva, M
pmc-13564768.description: Simple SummaryPancreatic cancer is one of the deadliest cancers, and accurate tumor delineation on contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) is essential for staging, treatment planning, and response assessment. Manual tumor segmentation is time-consuming and subject to reader variability. Recently, foundation models have shown promise for medical image segmentation, but their effectiveness for disease-specific tasks such as pancreatic tumor delineation remains uncertain.
